title: Guide - Calming an Anxious Heart - Receive His peace

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Calming an Anxious Heart. <short pause> This practice is called Receive His Peace. <short pause> You don't have to manufacture calm in these few minutes. <short pause> We are simply going to ask, give thanks, and make room to receive.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let yourself arrive where you are. <short pause> Notice the air on your skin, and the place where your body meets its support. <short pause> Let your face rest. <short pause> Breathe in gently... <short pause> and breathe out, with nothing to prove.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: When we are anxious, we often bargain with peace. <short pause> I'll rest when the results come back. <short pause> I'll relax when they call. <short pause> I'll be all right when this is over. <short pause> And so peace keeps moving further down the road... <short pause> always just past the next answer.

Paul knew about waiting for answers. <short pause> He was a prisoner when he wrote to his friends in Philippi, and he didn't know how his case would end. <short pause> Yet he offers them a peace that can begin before the answer comes. <short pause> We read it in Philippians, chapter four, verses six and seven.

Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. <long pause>

To be careful, in that older English, means to be full of care. <short pause> To be anxious. <short pause> Paul isn't scolding anyone for feeling that way. <short pause> He is showing us where the care can go. <short pause> Into prayer. Into asking. Into thanks.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So begin by asking. <short pause> You can be very simple and very specific. <short pause> Lord, please help me with... <short pause> and name what you need. <short pause> You don't have to choose careful words. <short pause> A request from a tired heart is still a request, and He hears it.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now, beside that request, set three small thanks. <short pause> One thing your senses can enjoy... a taste, a color, a warm place to sit. <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> One person who has been kind to you, even briefly. <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> One hard day, behind you now, that God has already brought you through. <short pause> Thank You.

Thanksgiving doesn't pretend the trouble is good. <short pause> It remembers that the trouble isn't all there is. <short pause> Your need is real. <short pause> And these gifts are real. <short pause> You can hold them both before God, without choosing between them.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: And then comes the promise. <short pause> The peace of God shall keep your hearts and minds. <short pause> The word keep is a guarding word, like a watch standing at a city gate. <short pause> You don't have to guard the peace. <short pause> His peace guards you.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So picture that gate, at the edge of your heart. <short pause> You have been standing there a long while, checking everything that approaches. <short pause> Now someone stronger has come to take the watch. <short pause> You can step back from the gate. <short pause> You can sit down. <short pause> Breathe in, and receive... <short pause> breathe out, and be kept.

This peace passes understanding, so it may not make sense yet. <short pause> Nothing may have been solved in the last few minutes. <short pause> You can be unfinished, and still be held. <short pause> You can be waiting, and still be at peace.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord Jesus, <short pause> thank You for hearing what I asked, and for every gift I named. <short pause> I receive the peace I cannot explain. <short pause> Stand watch over my heart where it aches, and over my mind where it circles. <short pause> Keep me, while I wait. <short pause> Amen.

As you return to what is next, you can leave the gate to Him. <short pause> When worry knocks, turn it into one honest request, and one small thanks. <short pause> And let His peace answer the door. <short pause> Go in peace.
